title: Microservices

validation.research: Lewis and Fowler's influential 2014 description establishes business capabilities, separate processes, independent deployment, and terminology without a universal service size. Richardson's architecture catalog supports the forces and distributed-operation tradeoffs; his Database per Service pattern distinguishes logical ownership from physical database hosting. Microsoft supports contract evolution, operational concerns, and conditional fault containment. Fowler supports deployment and monitoring prerequisites. Featonby's AWS article supports ambiguous timeouts, stable caller identities, equivalent responses, and atomic durable recording of identities with effects. The shop scenario, simulation, and illustrations are original teaching material.
validation.python_examples: All three actual article blocks run together and print pending 2, confirmed 2, confirmed 2 on separate lines. Checks pass for no cross-service implementation imports, JSON request and response values, uncertainty after a lost reply, pending state after a lost request, explicit retry and stable identities without repeated stock deduction, shortage and exact-stock boundaries, rejected-result replay after replenishment, invalid identities and units, conflicting identity reuse, response-copy isolation, terminal order states without extra calls, and surfaced malformed responses without false confirmation. An additive response field preserves caller behavior. A fresh subprocess verifies the same output after changing Inventory's private result representation while Orders and the demo remain byte-for-byte unchanged.

The new three-test integration suite also passes after tightening both alias-ID uniqueness assertions. Coverage includes canonical aliases, one primary collection, resolved related patterns, eight headings, exact highlighted code, responsive figures, asset dimensions, search, ten queries, revision hash, and concept marks.

The existing access-over-ownership article has no authored concept graphic. The other four graphics checks pass; unrelated coverage left untouched.

example_limits: A bounded serial in-memory simulation with a JSON transport test double, one caller and one product, manually repeated calls, and process-local remembered outcomes. It runs no network servers or independently deployed services. It implements no durable crash recovery, concurrent reservation, scoped authentication, automatic retry budget, cancellation, retention policy, cross-order ordering, global transaction, or exactly-once transport. Durable and concurrency-safe recording, caller-scoped identities, bounded retry policies, and reconciliation are explicit production responsibilities.
publication: Local implementation only. No publishing, deployment, push, or pull request.
